decisions.reason: The conditional-entropy formula used H_2 on a finite probability law without introducing that notation. Added H_2(p)=H_nat(p)/ln 2 and H_2(U)=H_2(P_U) in Definition and matching step 2.1; finite sums, zero-mass conventions and all rates are preserved.

The abstract hypotheses are intentionally stronger in scope than the title's finite-past application. Tail envelopes U_K decrease to zero in L1; Birkhoff and finite-measure L1 convergence preserve their integrals, so their decreasing limits vanish. The triangular error therefore tends to zero almost surely and in L1 without any information-specific hypothesis.

The telescoping proof establishes stationarity for every measurable alphabet, but its cited definition covered only finite alphabets. Preserved the unrestricted scope by specifying the measurable product space and citing the general measure-preserving and ergodicity definitions; the finite-alphabet convention remains explicitly compatible.

H_n is explicitly taken 'as in' the finite-block bit-entropy definition, and the owning page explicitly fixes all entropy rates in bits. Thus its uniform-reference KL identity is -H_n+log_2 N as written. Omitting the superscript locally does not change the defined unit. Updated only its contract quotation of the clarified supplier Definition.

The actual F3 supplier thm-stationary-entropy-rate-limit uses finite-block entropy from the bit definition, and its proof 3.1 identifies h with bit conditional entropies. F2 also uses bits, so H_n/n <= L_n*/n < H_n/n+1/n converges to h as claimed, including singleton support. Updated only its contract quotation of the clarified bit-entropy supplier.

The alleged missing mean identity is already proved in the supplier's Proof 5.1–6.1, so there is no mathematical gap. Review nevertheless confirmed a nonfatal source-citation defect: this item's Chapter 5/Theorem 6 thesis locator is wrong. Corrected it to Chapter 3, Theorem/Corollary 3.1 after inspecting the source, and made F1's precise supplier proof-step citation explicit.

F1's actual supplier explicitly records g_infinity in L1 in its Facts F1 and uses that integrability in Proof 2.1; its proved envelope supplier 5.1 establishes it directly. The corollary therefore applies finite-measure Birkhoff identification to a valid L1 input. AC, strict invariant measurability, integrability and all eventwise integral tests match the conditional-expectation definition.

The cited AEP lemma's actual Proof 3.1 already proves the strong converse: for epsilon>0 with R+epsilon<h, every success set has at most 2^floor(nR) words, so success <= P(I_n/n <= R+epsilon)+2^(-n epsilon), tending to zero. Its Statement's weaker summary does not invalidate this proved conclusion. Ergodic SMB and dominated convergence supply exactly the required probability AEP; equality R=h remains unclaimed.

The AEP coding supplier's Proof 3.1 explicitly proves success tends to zero below h using the success-set cardinality and the information threshold R+epsilon<h. The AMS AEP supplies convergence under P itself, and dominated convergence gives its in-probability form. Thus both strict-rate conclusions follow, with AC inherited explicitly and no stationarity imposed on P.
